text:
**Short answer:** for most people buying an 18650 charger, the **XTAR VC4SL** is the best pick. Nitecore's UMS4 is a close second.

## Top picks

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL (4-bay, USB-C)**
- It has four independent bays, takes cells from 10440 to 32650, and also charges NiMH and NiCd cells. Current is adjustable from 0.25A to 3A.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance per cell. It also has capacity-grading and storage modes. [1lumen's review](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/) found it handled a deeply drained 18650 and fit protected 21700s.
- Best Batteries rated it 4.3/5 and lists it at about $32.90 ([review and price link](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/)).
- Downsides: it doesn't list LiFePO4 support, and the cable is modest. A reviewer also saw it end NiMH charges early or mistake a NiMH cell for Li-ion ([Stephen Knight](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl)). That matters only if you charge NiMH. It also defaults to the highest current, so lower it for cells that can't take 3A.
- To get the fastest speeds you need a QC3.0 USB power source.

**Best for speed and LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4**
- It charges up to 3A in a single slot and 1A each with four cells (QC mode). It supports Li-ion, LiFePO4 and NiMH, shows battery health via internal resistance, and has reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection.
- Best Batteries lists it at about $38.95. Specs are on [Nitecore's page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4), and the [Best Batteries listing](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/) links to prices.
- Nitecore's page shows no included wall adapter, only a cable, so you'll need a USB source.

**Best budget 4-bay: Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics named it Editor's Choice. It has 4 independent bays, selectable 500mA or 1000mA charging, and an LCD, with a 4.6-star average across 4,608 reviews according to that site. It's also UL/CE/FCC certified.
- It lacks the grading and analysis features of the XTAR. [Review and Amazon link](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/).
- That site earns affiliate commissions, so I'd weigh its ranking accordingly.

**Cheapest simple option: Tenergy TN270 (2-bay), $18.99**
- It's a basic wall charger at 500mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input and has a 12-month warranty. [Buy at Tenergy (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger).

**Best for travel: IMREN 2-Bay USB-C**
- It charges at 1A per bay over USB-C and fits long protected 21700s. [Details here](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/).

## What to look for
- **Independent bays.** Each cell should be monitored and stopped on its own, not in pairs ([VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)).
- **Matching current to the cell.** Gentler charging, around 0.5C, is better for cell lifespan if you aren't in a hurry.
- **No-name chargers.** Avoid ones that don't say how they decide a cell is full.

I couldn't browse, so check current prices at checkout. If you tell me whether you need LiFePO4, 8 bays, or the lowest price, I can narrow it down.
